market_brief: Black Friday's half-day US session (closes 1pm ET) is set for a sharp AI-led rebound: Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 2.4-2.5% and S&P futures about 1.7-1.8% premarket, with Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Marvell (post-earnings) all higher, though the index is still on course for its worst month since 2022 (dashboard: Nasdaq 100 -10.1% 1M, SOX -18.6% 1M as of Wednesday). Rate risk has not gone away: futures put roughly 99% odds on a 25bp Fed hike on December 9 and the 10Y traded near 4.92%, above the 4.85% Wednesday print shown. Precious metals squeezed higher in thin trade (gold +4.7% to about $3,703 and silver +11.4% on the dashboard) after 52-week lows on Wednesday, while Asia closed strongly (Shanghai +3.7%, Kospi +4.3%, Nikkei +2.1%) and Europe extended its rally (Stoxx 600 +0.9%). India went the other way: Sensex fell 989 points (-1.17%) and Nifty 1.07% to 25,607 as IT sold off, crude stayed elevated and the rupee weakened to about 92.9 per dollar.
ai_brief: Markets dominate the AI story today: battered AI stocks including Nvidia and newly listed Anthropic rallied premarket after a brutal November, while analysis pieces focused on Anthropic trading around its $83 IPO price and a December 15 lockup expiry. On the product side, Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro is drawing attention as the strongest Chinese model on several benchmarks, Nvidia published Nemotron 3.5 Parse for document extraction, and OpenAI is reportedly testing a private-inference offering for businesses. Funding chatter centres on ElevenLabs, reportedly seeking a raise at about $33bn.

items.headline: AI stocks lead futures higher into Black Friday half-day; Nasdaq 100 futures up ~2.4%
items.summary: Nasdaq 100 futures rose about 2.4% and S&P 500 futures about 1.7% premarket as beaten-down chip names rebounded (Nvidia +4%, AMD +5%, Micron +6%). The Nasdaq 100 is still tracking its worst month since December 2022 after an ~8% November drop.

items.headline: Rebound comes despite near-certain December 9 Fed hike pricing
items.summary: CME FedWatch showed about 98.9% odds of a 25bp hike at the December meeting, and the 10-year yield traded near 4.92% premarket. Rising rates and AI worries were cited as twin drivers of November's tech selloff.

items.headline: Marvell up about 7% premarket after fiscal Q3 beat
items.summary: Marvell gained roughly 7% before the open after beating fiscal third-quarter expectations, joining a broad chip rebound. It was among the names that lost over 25% during November.

items.headline: Vertex falls 7% as FDA extends povetacicept review by up to three months
items.summary: The FDA pushed its decision on Vertex's IgA nephropathy drug povetacicept from November 30 to no later than February 28, 2027. Shares fell about 7.4% premarket to around $522.

items.headline: Alvotech drops ~10% after court blocks its Simponi biosimilar launch
items.summary: A federal court preliminarily enjoined Alvotech's proposed Simponi biosimilar in a suit brought by Janssen; Alvotech says it will appeal. Palo Alto Networks also slipped about 3% premarket.

items.headline: Anthropic shares hover near $83 IPO price; next lockup wave due December 15
items.summary: ANT closed Tuesday at $81.91 after an intraday low of $75.61, about 29% below its first-day high, and up to 303m more shares become eligible for sale on December 15 with further unlocks in January and February. It traded about 3.6% higher premarket Friday, back above the IPO price.

items.headline: Wide analyst spread on Anthropic: targets range from $59 (Hedgeye) to $300 (Arete)
items.summary: A Motley Fool write-up tallies a median Street target of about $137.50, with New Street at $105, Canaccord $135 and Melius $155, while noting the stock trades near 43x sales. It also cites a base rate that large US IPOs typically dip well below their offer price in year one.

items.headline: Sensex sinks 989 points, Nifty ends at 25,607 as IT, crude and rupee weigh
items.summary: Sensex fell 1.17% to 83,339 and Nifty 1.07% to 25,607, the first weekly loss in five weeks, with HCL Tech, Infosys and TCS down 2.5-2.8%. Brokers blamed elevated crude, a rupee near 92.9 and higher bond yields, and one strategist flagged flows rotating to rebounding Asian AI stocks. (Update to this morning's midday slide.)

items.headline: Bosch India sets Dec 23 record date for 1:5 split and 1:3 bonus; BEL tops Sensex gainers
items.summary: Bosch fixed December 23 as the record date for its split and bonus issue. Metals outperformed (Nifty Metal +1.4%) while broader midcap and smallcap indices ended slightly higher despite the benchmark fall.

items.headline: Update: China closes strong after support pledge — Shanghai +3.7%, Shenzhen +6.3%
items.summary: Following this morning's report of State Council support, Chinese indices closed near session highs, with the Shenzhen Component up about 6.3% and the Hang Seng 2.1%. The rally added to a broad Asian rebound led by chipmakers.

items.headline: Europe extends rally; ECB minutes show many members open to an October hike
items.summary: The Stoxx 600 rose about 0.9% Friday, heading for a weekly gain near 1.8% but a monthly loss of roughly 1.5%. Short-dated euro yields rose after the ECB's meeting account indicated a large number of members could have backed a hike in October (per a secondary, AI-rewritten report).

items.headline: Lumibird jumps about 18% on Thales deal
items.summary: French laser maker Lumibird surged at the open on a deal with Thales, while chipmakers and miners led European gains into midday.

items.headline: Gold rebounds ~4% from 52-week low; silver up double digits in thin holiday trade
items.summary: COMEX gold rose about 4% to roughly $3,708 after Wednesday's 52-week low near $3,425, and silver jumped more than 10% (dashboard: gold +4.7%, silver +11.4%). MCX gold and silver futures in India rose 2.6% and 5.3%. Moves came despite firm yields and hike pricing.

items.headline: Update: Brent near $97 front-month, WTI ~$86 into Sunday's OPEC+ meeting
items.summary: Brent was about $97 and WTI up 2.6% near $86 on Hormuz shipping and Saudi infrastructure risks, setting up a first weekly gain in a month. The dashboard's Brent -2.3% to $92.45 likely reflects a roll to the February contract (Feb Brent was quoted near $92.3), not a sell-off.

items.headline: Prediction markets: Kalshi shows ~93% odds of a 25bp December Fed hike
items.summary: Kalshi's Fed market prices a quarter-point hike on December 9 as the overwhelming favourite, roughly in line with futures; prediction-market trackers put a 50bp move at a high-single-digit probability.

items.headline: Week framing: S&P 500 up nearly 4% for the week heading into the half-day
items.summary: Despite the November slump, the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Dow were each up roughly 4% on the week as of Wednesday plus futures, helped by Nvidia's surge after Jensen Huang's return as CEO on Monday.

items.headline: Calendar: OPEC+ Nov 29; India Q2 GDP Nov 30; RBI Dec 4; Anthropic lockup Dec 15; FOMC Dec 8-9; ECB Dec 17
items.summary: US cash markets close at 1pm ET today. Next week brings OPEC+ baselines (Sunday), India GDP (Monday), Huang's congressional appearances (Dec 1 and 3) and the RBI decision (Dec 4), with the Fed meeting and the next ANT unlock to follow.

items.headline: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro claims gains over K3 on 14 of 17 benchmarks
items.summary: Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it says beats K3 on most of its benchmark suite; coverage positions it as the strongest Chinese model and close to leading US models on coding. Reports say cyber-related training data was stripped from it.

items.headline: AI shares including Nvidia and Anthropic rebound premarket after November rout
items.summary: Anthropic rose about 3.6% premarket to around $85.7 and Nvidia about 4%, alongside Micron, SanDisk and Oracle, after a month in which several AI bellwethers fell over 25%.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing shows ~$900bn of compute commitments; Q3 revenue ~$17bn
items.summary: Per its 424B4 prospectus as summarised by TokenPost, Anthropic reported Q3 revenue of about $16.96bn with a $567m operating loss, and roughly $900.9bn of procurement commitments and leases as of September 30.

items.headline: Nvidia publishes Nemotron 3.5 Parse document-extraction model with open data and recipe
items.summary: Nvidia detailed Nemotron 3.5 Parse for extracting content from document images, releasing synthetic chart/table data, a fine-tuning recipe and a DFlash2 speculative-decoding companion.

items.headline: llama.cpp launches weekly automated AMD Ryzen/Radeon benchmark dashboard
items.summary: The ggml team began publishing automated llama-bench results for AMD hardware such as the Radeon AI Pro R9700, following this week's community fork that sped up prefill on the same card.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly testing 'Private Inference' for business prompts
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly piloting a private-inference option aimed at enterprises worried about who can see their prompts and data; details on pricing and availability were not confirmed.

items.headline: ElevenLabs reportedly seeking funding at about a $33bn valuation
items.summary: Voice-AI firm ElevenLabs is reportedly in talks to raise at roughly $33bn, triple its $11bn February valuation, per Sifted as cited in an AI leaders briefing.

items.headline: Mistral opens Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore
items.summary: Mistral announced a Singapore hub for Asia-Pacific; Thinking Machines' open-weights Inkling 2 Mini laptop model also featured in this week's roundups.

items.headline: Google Cloud to require AI agents to reach Workspace via secure interfaces from Feb 2027
items.summary: Google will route agent access to Workspace through its MCP servers and CLI with Model Armor protections and reject non-agent OAuth clients, per Infosecurity Magazine as summarised in a daily digest.

items.headline: FDA clears DeepHealth's Mammo Risk AI for 3-5 year breast-cancer risk prediction
items.summary: The tool predicts near-term breast-cancer risk from existing 3D mammograms and was trained on about 220,000 studies; a new CPT Category III code takes effect January 1, 2027.

items.headline: Hacker News picks: browser tabs as a container runtime, open dispatcher for coding agents
items.summary: Developer chatter featured tabc, which runs OCI containers in browser tabs on a WebAssembly Linux kernel, and Hub, an open-source dispatcher for Claude Code and Codex sessions via browser or Telegram.
